1.why: Recovery records store sessionId at creation and /api/recovery-verify rejects use when record.sessionId !== session.id, so the code is checked against the requesting user/session.

2.why: Tokens are bound to the session that requested them (record lookup via session.recovery and sessionId comparison), so the same code cannot be used by any other user/session.

3.why: Nothing in /api/password invalidates other sessions; existing authenticated sessions remain valid until their 8-hour expiry after a reset.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and an HSTS header, but the TLS protocol version is not explicitly pinned to the latest version.

5.why: Reset codes and passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes via Bun.password.hash (cost 10), which is the appropriate protection algorithm.

6.why: The simulated delivery message contains only the recovery code and generic text ('If the details match an account...'), exposing no other private user data.

7.why: cleanText rejects control characters and angle brackets, validIdentifier enforces a strict character whitelist, and client rendering escapes via esc()/textContent.

8.why: Client navigation is restricted to a validRoutes whitelist and server 'next' values are fixed internal paths, so no user-controlled or external redirects exist.

9.why: No email templates exist; simulated messages render through textContent and all dynamic HTML is escaped and served under a nonce-based CSP.

10.why: The visible log panel and API responses deliberately expose secrets, e.g. log('[SIMULATED DELIVERY] Current browser recovery code: '+out.testToken) and testMfaCode in the login response.

11.why: Runtime storage uses bcrypt, but the initial password 'Welcome!2025Heart' and MFA code '246810' are hardcoded directly in the source code.

12.why: The account is initialized with the hardcoded, known password 'Welcome!2025Heart', which functions as a default credential.

13.why: Failed logins (5), recovery requests (3), code verifications (5), and MFA attempts (5) all trigger timed lockouts via the throttle maps and lockUntil.

14.why: Login and recovery responses are generic and identical, but the password step's distinct error for non-existent accounts and the short-circuited bcrypt timing slightly reveal account existence.

15.why: Reset codes are 32-byte crypto.randomBytes tokens, stored only hashed, single-use, 15-minute expiry, and bound to the requesting session.
